question: Which attention heads and low-dimensional activation subspaces implement in-context inference of an integer-addition rule in instruction-tuned LLMs?

key_findings.claim: Sparse optimization and subsequent ablation localize most add-k task-vector performance to three attention heads in Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
key_findings.evidence: A coefficient optimization first selects 33 of 1,024 heads; mean ablation separates formatting from k-specific content and leaves three dominant heads. Their combined intervention retains about 90% of original ICL accuracy, while individual scaling tests show much weaker alternatives.

key_findings.claim: Each dominant head's task vector is well approximated by a six-dimensional subspace with periodic and magnitude directions.
key_findings.evidence: Projection onto six principal directions gives intervention accuracy 0.76 versus 0.79 before projection. Four fitted directions track the units digit through periods 2, 5, and 10; two lower-frequency directions track magnitude or tens information.

key_findings.claim: An exact attention algebra maps output-token aggregator subspaces back to label-token extractor subspaces.
key_findings.evidence: The paper applies the output projection and attention weights to derive corresponding input-position directions. Mixed-demonstration experiments show label tokens contributing signals related to y_i-x_i rather than merely copying the final answer.

key_findings.claim: Later demonstrations can suppress erroneous contributions from earlier examples, which the authors interpret as self-correction.
key_findings.evidence: When examples share one rule, extracted signals increasingly align with the aggregate task vector; conflicting or corrupted demonstrations reveal position-dependent suppression. The behavior is demonstrated on a narrow synthetic family and does not establish a general correction algorithm for natural tasks.

method.core_idea: Compress a concrete ICL computation from model-wide behavior to a few heads and then to interpretable low-dimensional directions.
method.mechanism: Elicit add-k task vectors, optimize sparse head coefficients, mean-ablate heads, use PCA and periodic basis fits on retained activations, derive extractor/aggregator subspace identities, and intervene on activations to measure retained task accuracy.
assumptions: Add-k prompts isolate a representative in-context-learning mechanism.
Function-vector interventions measure task information rather than generic formatting.
PCA directions and hand-interpreted trigonometric rotations recover causally relevant structure.
Mean ablation is an appropriate counterfactual for irrelevant head content.
The selected prompts and integer range adequately sample periodic structure.

techniques.role: Optimizes a small set of heads whose summed outputs act as a task vector.
Distinguishes k-specific information from formatting support.
Compresses each important head to six dimensions.
Identifies period-2, period-5, period-10, and magnitude coordinates.
Traces final-token task directions back to demonstration label tokens.

evaluations.result: Three heads retain about 90% of original ICL accuracy
evaluations.baseline: All 1,024 heads and the initial 33-head sparse set

evaluations.result: Label-token directions encode individual differences and later consistent examples suppress earlier mistakes

limitations: Author-stated: final qualitative subspace interpretation still requires human judgment.
Reviewer-identified: the main mechanistic claim is centered on one model family and a highly structured addition task.
Reviewer-identified: head selection and mean ablation can miss distributed backup circuits.
Reviewer-identified: 0.76 versus 0.79 intervention accuracy leaves nonzero unexplained behavior and does not measure all original task performance.
Reviewer-identified: trigonometric basis fits are selected after visualization and need held-out confirmatory tests.
failure_modes: A different prompt format recruits different heads.
Backup heads compensate under ablation and obscure the native circuit.
Periodic coordinates alias outside the sampled integer range.
Subspace correlations decode k but are not used causally by downstream computation.
A natural ICL task lacks a single low-dimensional task variable.
reusable_insights: Localize components before interpreting directions inside them.
Quantify how much behavior survives every compression step.
Trace an output subspace algebraically back through attention to candidate source tokens.
Use conflicting demonstrations to distinguish extraction, aggregation, and correction mechanisms.
Confirm hand-discovered periodic bases on preregistered ranges and models.
open_questions: Do the same heads and directions generalize across Llama checkpoints and other architectures?
How do carries and multiple-digit outputs compose across layers?
Can an automated method discover the periodic basis without visual inspection?
Are self-correction weights learned for reliability or induced by recency and attention normalization?
Which natural-language ICL tasks admit similarly compact task subspaces?

competitive_landscape.title: Language Models Use Trigonometry to Do Addition
competitive_landscape.difference: Kantamneni and Tegmark find helical or trigonometric number representations in ordinary addition. This paper discovers related periodic coordinates specifically in task vectors for in-context rule inference and traces them across attention positions.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Addition in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Quirke and Barez reverse-engineer trained-transformer addition algorithms and interventions. The present work studies inference of a varying add-k rule from demonstrations in a pretrained LLM rather than fixed arithmetic computation alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Which Attention Heads Matter for In-Context Learning?
competitive_landscape.difference: Yin and Steinhardt study selecting causally important ICL heads across tasks. The present paper adds within-head low-dimensional decomposition and an extractor-to-aggregator identity for one arithmetic family.

competitive_landscape.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
competitive_landscape.difference: Olsson et al. connect induction heads to generic pattern completion and ICL emergence. This paper identifies a different, task-vector-style circuit for extracting and aggregating a numerical rule in a mature instruction-tuned model.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A few heads and six-dimensional periodic subspaces implement add-k in-context learning, with an algebraic extractor/aggregator relation revealing self-correction.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sparse selection, ablation, projection, intervention, mixed-example prompts, and exact attention identities support a detailed case study.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Trigonometric arithmetic codes, function vectors, and ICL heads have clear predecessors. The novel synthesis is unusually fine-grained localization of a demonstration-derived arithmetic rule and tracing it from label tokens to the final task vector. Generality beyond this task and model remains open.

reviewer_notes: Read all 36 extracted pages, including main interventions, equations, discussion, references, and extended PCA/extraction plots. Four primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23. Reported accuracies and dimensions were passage-checked; no independent intervention run was executed.
